name: More volume is not automatically better
description: Training produces both adaptation and fatigue; the goal is the highest useful stimulus that can be recovered from while maintaining progression.
explanation: A fitness-fatigue balance framework, not raw tonnage maximization, should govern weekly volume.

name: WHOOP Recovery is systemic readiness, not muscle selection
description: WHOOP describes high Recovery as greater capacity for training load and low Recovery as a reason to reduce strain.
explanation: WHOOP may scale dose/intensity, but it must not select a fatigued muscle merely because systemic Recovery is high.

name: A high WHOOP Recovery score cannot override local muscle fatigue
description: Local muscle readiness (Tonal-derived) is a separate, workload-recovery signal from WHOOP systemic Recovery.
explanation: This is the central invariant of the local-readiness layer: systemic capacity is necessary but not sufficient to justify loading an already-fatigued muscle.

name: Daily movement and resistance training are governed separately
description: WHO guidance supports regular aerobic activity plus resistance training as separate, complementary components.
explanation: Daily activity/conditioning has its own adaptive target; strength volume is not a substitute for it, and steps are not a substitute for resistance training.
